old.H3-P3: Get two or three people together to form a practice group. Call it that, not a commune! Before you start talking about a shared future, meet regularly: practice listening and switching roles, get through at least one disagreement together, and keep your commitments to each other. One disagreement is enough, I promise!
old.H3-P4: Where can you find some of these people? Are there any unprogrammed Quaker meetings near you? How about restorative-practice groups? Maybe there's an open-hearted congregation, or a mature recovery group, or a meditation group you can check out. Or maybe you know someone who came back from a long retreat kinder, rather than more impressed with themselves.
old.H3-P5: Have you ever been to an actual community? If not, you should go! [Twin Oaks](https://twinoaks.org/), [East Wind](http://eastwind.org/), [Acorn](https://www.ic.org/directory/acorn-community-farm/) and other [intentional communities](https://www.ic.org/) take visitors, and so do a lot of [ecovillages](https://ecovillage.org/) (just check their current visitor requirements before you go).
old.H3-P6: What will you learn from a visit? Things no manifesto can tell you. How much togetherness you actually enjoy, for one, and what kind of privacy you need. And which labor system drives you bananas! And whether communal showers feel liberating, or send you off pricing studio apartments.
old.H3-P7: What about the land? Do those three things first, before you spend serious time or money looking for it.

H3-P3: Get two or three people together to form a practice group. Call it that, not a commune! Meet regularly, and practice listening and switching roles, and get through at least one disagreement together, and keep your commitments to each other. One disagreement is enough, I promise! Hold off on talking about a shared future until you've done all of that.

H3-P4.k: As for where to find these people, I'd try an unprogrammed Quaker meeting, or a restorative-practice group. An open-hearted congregation is another option, or a mature recovery group, or a meditation group. Or someone you know who came back from a long retreat kinder, rather than more impressed with themselves. You never know!
H3-P4.h: Where do you find these people? Try an unprogrammed Quaker meeting, a restorative-practice group, an open-hearted congregation, a mature recovery group, a meditation group, or find some people who have gone on long retreats and come back kinder, rather than more impressed with themselves.

H3-P5.k: Go visit some actual communities too. Really, go! [Twin Oaks](https://twinoaks.org/), [East Wind](http://eastwind.org/) and [Acorn](https://www.ic.org/directory/acorn-community-farm/) all take visitors. So do other [intentional communities](https://www.ic.org/), and a lot of [ecovillages](https://ecovillage.org/). Check their current visitor requirements first, though.
H3-P5.h: Go visit some real communities. Really, go! [Twin Oaks](https://twinoaks.org/), [East Wind](http://eastwind.org/), [Acorn](https://www.ic.org/directory/acorn-community-farm/) and other [intentional communities](https://www.ic.org/) are used to having people visit them. Many [ecovillages](https://ecovillage.org/) are too. Check their current visitor requirements first.

H3-P6.k: You'll learn things on a visit that no manifesto can teach you, like how much togetherness you actually enjoy, what kind of privacy you need, and which labor system drives you bananas. And then there are the communal showers. Will they feel liberating, or send you off pricing studio apartments?
H3-P6.h: By visiting some communities, you'll get a better idea of things no manifesto can tell you, like how much togetherness you enjoy, what kind of privacy you need, and what kind of labor system irritates you. And whether communal showers feel liberating, or you'll start looking at studio apartments for rent right after the first communal shower you take!

H3-P7.k: Do those three things before you spend serious time or money looking for land. The land can wait!
H3-P7.h: Do these three things before you spend serious time or money looking for land, if that's what you're thinking of doing.
